cim: Air Charter Association Forum Assesses Artificial Intelligence Impact
cim_eredeti: Air Charter Association Forum Assesses Artificial Intelligence Impact
szoveg_eredeti:
The Air Charter Association (ACA) held its annual Broker & Operator Forum on Thursday with the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) topping the agenda. The event at the Royal Aeronautical Society in London attracted more than 60 senior industry executives.

The first of two panel discussions assessed how the role of charter brokers may change as AI tools become more widely used. In a survey conducted during the event, 79% of attendees confirmed they are already using AI in the broking or sales processes. At the same time, 67% said they believe the rise of AI will increase the need for a “personal, trusted service,” with trust identified as the single most important value a broker provides for clients.

During the forum, David Kendrick, head of airline licensing with the consumer and markets group at the UK Civil Aviation Authority, answered questions about industry concerns over operator permit processes for the UK and overseas territories, plus cabotage rules. This was followed by a panel discussion on maintaining best practices through the ACA’s new member accreditation system.

“The Broker & Operator Forum is always a great opportunity for debate and the perfect platform to bring brokers and operators together to discuss industry matters,” ACA chief executive Glenn Hogben said.
